speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are presenting with a generalized nonpruritic rash, a recent high fever, and a seizure. To begin my assessment, please tell me your age and when you first noticed the fever.

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Measles (Rubeola).

The clinical picture of a high fever followed by a generalized nonpruritic rash starting on the trunk and spreading outward, combined with a history of a seizure likely caused by fever, is classic for measles. I will proceed with confirming this diagnosis based on the temporal progression and rash characteristics provided.
